newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian weekly OTC volume, turnover fall.
newsitem.headline: Croatian weekly OTC volume, turnover fall.

text.p: Croatian over-the-counter (OTC) stocks turnover fell to 4.2 million kuna in the week to March 21 from almost 6.3 million kuna a week earlier.
Weekly volume shrank to 13,098 from 16,915 units as 32 firms -- mostly hoteliers, banks and shippers -- traded on the OTC market in Varazdin and its outpost in Osijek in eastern Croatia.
In a spillover from the central bourse in Zagreb which also saw mosts stocks prices falling, 17 issues fell, only two rose, 10 ended flat and three were traded for the first time.
Food stock Podravka was the most active with a total of 4,918 shares sold. It closed unchanged at 306 kuna after rising to 315 earlier in the week.
It was followed by textile firm Varteks, selling 1,416 shares to close 11.11 percent weaker at 80 kuna.
The biggest loser was tourist group Hoteli Rabac, which dipped 13.04 percent to 100 kuna on a small volume of 45 shares.
Rijeka's repair docks Viktor Lenac was the bigger of two gainers, rising 22.50 percent to 196 kuna with 126 units changing hands.
